note: Ground of a 1891-1943 prefecture that the 1920 町村 of N03-1920 do not hold, added to it from another atom set (scripts/histrecon/annex.mjs, applied by scripts/build-hist-admin-recon.mjs to the record whose KEY names this file). N03-1920 was compiled on the 1950 municipalities, so it carries no 町村 north-east of Etorofu: the Kuril Islands from Urup to Shumshu, Japanese from the Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1875) to the Soviet occupation of 1945, were part of 北海道庁 and are drawn by data/cshapes.js in Japan (scripts/cshapes/review.json kuril-1875) while no first-level unit covered them. An atom is taken only when its whole outer ring lies inside `within`, the treaty's ground; a polygon partly inside fails the build. Applied to the assembler's finished spans, so it does not re-key the assembler's cached unions.

annex.withinIs: The Kuril group north-east of the Friza (Vries) Strait up to the strait between Cape Lopatka and Shumshu — the same ring as scripts/cshapes/review.json kuril-1875; Etorofu (Iturup, already a 町村 of N03-1920) and Kamchatka lie outside.
annex.fact: By the Treaty of Saint Petersburg (7 May 1875, in force 22 August 1875) the eighteen islands from Shumshu to Urup became Japanese; the Kaitakushi placed them in 千島国 as 占守郡, 新知郡 and 得撫郡 (1876), and from 1886-01-26 they were part of 北海道庁, administered through 根室支庁 from 1897. They remained so until the Soviet occupation of August-September 1945. In 1891-1943 the first-level unit of this ground is therefore 北海道庁; 千島国 and 根室国 were geographic provinces inside it, not first-level units.

cite.cite: Treaty of Saint Petersburg (Treaty for the Exchange of Sakhalin for the Kuril Islands), 7 May 1875, Article 2
